_doc: Crons that are HELD: a kill file is present on node-8 under /etc/hydra, placed by a human for a reason the
file itself states. scripts/check-held-cron-guard.py (pre-commit + PR Validation) refuses any diff that
sets enabled:true on one of these, changes its schedule or payload, or deletes its row - and refuses any
added code line that deletes a .disabled sentinel. The only way a held cron moves is the recorded step:
a PR that removes its entry here AND cites the step's evidence key ([key=kill-lift-MMDD-HHMM], written
by scripts/credit-approve-hold-lift.sh) on a commit-message line naming that cron, or
HELD_CRON_LIFT_KEY=kill-lift-MMDD-HHMM:<cron-name> at commit time, AND commits the executed step's
record at data/kill-lift/<key>.evidence; the rules (R1-R6) are the guard's docstring. Why: on 2026-11-07 an automated review fix flipped
credit-trust-score-approve-15m to enabled:true inside a print-only PR (hydra#1832, dd40d67e9); it was
caught by a human and reverted. A pin on the value catches today's file; this registry plus the guard
refuses the change at the gate. On a host where /etc/hydra exists the guard ALSO treats every cron whose
description names a present kill file as held, so an entry missing here is a warning, not a loophole.

held.name: credit-trust-decide-15m
held.why: never-lower refusal: the coded-decider output could not be invalidated after a failed refresh ([Errno 13] Permission denied); lifted only with credit-trust-score-approve.disabled in the same recorded step

held.name: credit-trust-verify-notify-15m
held.why: the verify-request sender is retired (docs/credit-verification/verify-request-notes.md); its row stays disabled

held.name: credit-past-verify-wave-15m
held.why: same sender, same kill file as credit-trust-verify-notify-15m

held.name: uvn-ticket-popularity-under30
held.why: held on the host; its row stays disabled until the kill file's owner lifts it
